cardDetailedText:
MV Hondius departs Ushuaia, Argentina on 1 April 2026. Oceanwide Expeditions notes that the itinerary is the Atlantic Odyssey voyage, which was scheduled to end in Praia, Cape Verde, on 4 May 2026. They note that guests can book the cruise as Ushuaia-to-Saint Helena, or Ushuaia-to-Cabo Verde.

Oceanwide reports that the vessel departed with 175 individuals onboard (114 guests, 61 crew). This includes all individuals currently identified as outbreak cases.

Case #1 develops respiratory symptoms.

Symptom onset date is initially reported as April 6 by WHO. A later *NEJM* article reports onset as April 3 without clarifying the discrepancy.

sources.label: NEJM: Andes Hantavirus Outbreak on a Cruise Ship, 2026

cardTitle: MV Hondius arrives in South Georgia

cardDetailedText: Case #1 passes away onboard the MV Hondius on 11 April. No microbiological tests were performed.

cardTitle: MV Hondius arrives in Tristan da Cunha
cardDetailedText: Oceanwide reports that one crew member disembarked at this port.
location: Tristan da Cunha, British Overseas Territory

cardDetailedText: Case #8, an adult male, disembarks in Tristan da Cunha on 14 April.

cardTitle: MV Hondius departs Tristan da Cunha
cardDetailedText: Oceanwide reports that 6 guests embarked  at this portand the vessel departed with 180 individuals onboard (120 guests, 60 crew).
location: Tristan da Cunha, British Overseas Territory

cardTitle: MV Hondius arrives in and departs Gough Island
MV Hondius arrives in Saint Helena
cardDetailedText: Oceanwide reports that 32 guests disembarked at this port, including the deceased individual (Case #1) and their spouse accompanying the body (Case #2).

Case #3, an adult male, develops symptoms (shortness of breath, fever).

Symptom onset date is initially reported as April 24 by WHO. A later *NEJM* article reports onset as April 21 without clarifying the discrepancy.

sources.label: NEJM: Andes Hantavirus Outbreak on a Cruise Ship, 2026

cardDetailedText: Case #7 disembarks at Saint Helena on 22 April.
Case #2 goes ashore at Saint Helena with gastrointestinal symptoms.
Oceanwide reports that 1 crew member embarked at this port and the vessel departed with 149 individuals onboard (88 guests, 61 crew).
Case #2 is reported to have deteriorated on a flight to Johannesburg, South Africa, on 25 April.
Case #2 passes away on 26 April in a Johannesburg clinic.
Case #6, an adult male working as a ship guide reports onset of symptoms on 27 April with mild respiratory and gastrointestinal symptoms.

cardTitle: MV Hondius arrives in and departs Ascension Island
cardDetailedText: Oceanwide reports that two guests disembarked (medically evacuated): one symptomatic British national (Case #3) and one asymptomatic American national (their partner). The vessel departed with 147 individuals onboard (86 guests, 61 crew).
Case #3  was disembarked and medically evacuated from Ascension Island on 27 April and was hospitalised in an Intensive Care Unit (ICU) in Johannesburg, South Africa.
location: Ascension Island, British Oversea Territory; Johannesburg, South Africa

cardDetailedText: Case #7 flies back to Switzerland on 27-28 April, through South Africa and Qatar.
Case #4, an adult female, develops symptoms (fever and general malaise) on 28 April.
Case #8 experiences onset of symptoms on 28 April with diarrhoea and two days later with fever.
Case #5, an adult male working as the ship doctor, reported onset of symptoms on 30 April, including fever, fatigue, muscle pain, and mild respiratory symptoms.
Case #7 starts experiencing symptoms on 1 May after arrival in Switzerland, where he immediately self-isolated and reported to local public health authorities.

On 2 May 2026, WHO receives notification from the National IHR Focal Point of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland (hereafter referred to as the United Kingdom) regarding a cluster of severe acute respiratory illness, including two deaths and one critically ill passenger, aboard a Dutch-flagged cruise ship.
Pan-hantavirus RT-PCR testing (from Case #3) confirms hantavirus as the causative agent.

sources.label: NEJM: Andes Hantavirus Outbreak on a Cruise Ship, 2026

cardDetailedText: Case #4 develops pneumonia and passes away on 2 May.

cardTitle: MV Hondius arrives near Praia, Cabo Verde
cardDetailedText: The vessel was anchored offshore and was not permitted to dock. Cabo Verde argued that it was too small a country to handle the outbreak.

sources.label: New York Times: How a Nature Cruise Turned Into a Nightmare, 16 May 2026

cardDetailedText: WHO reports 7 cases (2 confirmed, 5 suspected) and 3 deaths.
Specimens from Case #2 and Case #3 are confirmed positive for Andes virus via sequencing at the National Institute for Communicable Diseases in South Africa.

sources.label: NEJM: Andes Hantavirus Outbreak on a Cruise Ship, 2026

cardTitle: Case #7 confirmed positive for Andes virus
cardDetailedText: Specimens from Case #7 are confirmed positive for Andes virus.

sources.label: NEJM: Andes Hantavirus Outbreak on a Cruise Ship, 2026

cardDetailedText: On May 6, 2026, WHO confirmed that the type of hantavirus responsible for this outbreak is the Andes virus.

cardTitle: Multiple passengers are evacuated to the Netherlands
cardDetailedText: On 6 May, three individuals were transferred by medicalized aircraft from *MV Hondius* to the Netherlands. Two listed as guests and one listed as crew. Case #5 is among those evacuated.

cardTitle: MV Hondius departs Praia, Cabo Verde
cardDetailedText: Oceanwide reports that four medical staff (counted as guests) embarked and the vessel departed with 147 individuals onboard (87 guests, 60 crew).
Case #6 is medically evacuated to the Netherlands on 7 May.

cardTitle: Case #5 confirmed positive for Andes virus
cardDetailedText: Specimens from Case #5 are confirmed positive for Andes virus.

sources.label: NEJM: Andes Hantavirus Outbreak on a Cruise Ship, 2026

cardDetailedText: WHO reports 8 cases (6 confirmed, 2 probable) and 3 deaths.

cardTitle: Case #6 confirmed positive for Andes virus
cardDetailedText: Specimens from Case #6 are confirmed positive for Andes virus.

sources.label: NEJM: Andes Hantavirus Outbreak on a Cruise Ship, 2026

cardTitle: MV Hondius Arrives in Canary Islands
cardDetailedText: On 10 May, the ship arrives in the Canary Islands, Spain, where disembarkation began.  Passengers and most of the crew are repatriated from the Canary Islands to their respective residence countries or transit points via specially arranged non-commercial flights, with WHO and partners supporting the disembarkation process. Case #9, Case #10, and Case #11 depart the *MV Hondius* at this point.

sources.label: NEJM: Andes Hantavirus Outbreak on a Cruise Ship, 2026

cardDetailedText: WHO reports that contact tracing efforts include passengers who disembarked in Saint Helena, United Kingdom, on 24 April; Praia, Cabo Verde, on 6 May; and Tenerife, Spain, on 10 and 11 May.

cardTitle: Canadian Passengers return to British Columbia
cardDetailedText: Four Canadian passengers from the MV Hondius arrive in British Columbia via a chartered aircraft. These include a couple in their 70s from the Yukon, a Vancouver Island resident in their 70s, and another individual from BC in their 50s. All individuals are asymptomatic and will initiate a 21-42 day self-isolation period on Vancouver Island.

sources.label: BC Provincial Health Officer Statement, 10 May 2026

NEJM: Andes Hantavirus Outbreak on a Cruise Ship, 2026

cardDetailedText: The ship leaves the Canary Islands on 11 May and is sailing to the Netherlands, with 25 crew members remaining on board, along with two Dutch health and care workers to conduct their health monitoring and provide any healthcare that may be necessary.

cardTitle: Case #9 and Case #10 confirmed positive for Andes virus
cardDetailedText: Specimens from Case #9 and Case #10 are confirmed positive for Andes virus.

sources.label: NEJM: Andes Hantavirus Outbreak on a Cruise Ship, 2026
NEJM: Andes Hantavirus Outbreak on a Cruise Ship, 2026

cardDetailedText: WHO reports 11 cases (8 confirmed, 2 probable, 1 inconclusive) and 3 deaths.

Canadian Chief Public Health Officer Dr. Joss Reimer reports that there are a total of nine individuals within Canada who are identified as high-risk contacts with potential exposures to Andes hantavirus: Four Canadian passengers aboard the MV Hondius who arrived in British Columbia on May 10; Two individuals who were aboard the MV Hondius, disembarked prior to the outbreak being identified, and were on a flight where they could have been exposed to a confirmed case; Three individuals who were on a flight where they may have been exposed to a confirmed case. Dr. Reimer identified a further 26 individuals deemed to have minimal risk who have been referred to provincial/territorial authorities for follow up. These individuals were on one or more flights with a case, but there is no evidence of any direct or prolonged contact. The flights in question are: St. Helena to Johannesburg; Johannesburg to Amsterdam.

sources.label: Speaking Remarks for the Chief Public Health Officer, 14 May 2026
CBC News: 26 more Canadians being contacted for 'low-risk' hantavirus exposure, 14 May 2026

cardDetailedText: PHAC reports that an individual (Case 11) had was transported to hospital for assessment after developing mild symptoms (fever, headache). This individual is one of four high-risk individuals who was already self-isolating and being monitored for symptoms. This is an individual in their 70s from the Yukon, who had been a passenger on MV Hondius and was already in self-isolation in British Columbia.

sources.label: CBC News: National lab confirms hantavirus case for Canadian cruise passenger isolating in B.C., 17 May 2026

cardTitle: WHO Reports 10 cases, 3 deaths; inconclusive case re-classified
cardDetailedText: WHO reports 10 cases (8 confirmed, 2 probable) and 3 deaths. One inconclusive case from the previous update tested negative and is no longer considered a case.

sources.label: CIPRAP: Hantavirus outbreak reduced to 10 cases as ship passengers return to home countries, 15 May 2026

cardDetailedText: PHAC reports that an individual (Case 11) had a sample test presumptively positive for hantavirus after developing mild symptoms earlier in the week. This individual is one of four high-risk individuals who was already self-isolating and being monitored for symptoms. This is an individual in their 70s from the Yukon, who had been a passenger on MV Hondius and was already in self-isolation in British Columbia.

cardTitle: MV Hondius arrives in Rotterdam, The Netherlands
cardDetailedText: The MV Hondius arrives in Rotterdam, The Netherlands for disinfection. The ship was carrying 25 crew members, two medical personnel, and no passengers. 20 crew members and the two medical personnel left the ship and were taken to a quarantine facility.

sources.label: CBC News: Hantavirus-stricken cruise ship docks in the Netherlands for disinfection, 18 May 2026
